newsitem.title: FRANCE: French bill to restrict layoffs before end of year.
newsitem.headline: French bill to restrict layoffs before end of year.

text.p: France's new left-wing government said on Wednesday it would propose legislation tightening restrictions on layoffs by companies before the end of the year.

Government spokeswoman Catherine Trautmann told reporters after a cabinet meeting the bill would re-establish the requirement for state labour inspectors to authorise redundancies, abolished by a right-wing government in 1986.

Prime Minister Lionel Jospin said in a speech to parliament on June 19 he would review existing legislation and propose changes to improve protection for workers and end legal uncertainty for companies.
"From the moment I took office, I was confronted with the consequences of the Vilvoorde (Renault Belgian plant closure) conflict. I do not want to see this situation repeated," Jospin said.
"Job cuts should be a last resort after the end of genuine negotiations," he added.
Jospin's left-wing government swept to power in June 1 parliamentary elections.
Trautmann said Jospin wanted "to put and end to the abruptness, lack of vision and incompetence with which these highly sensitive cases were handled previously".
The draft legislation would "redefine the administrative framework in which layoffs take place", she said.

"There is a desire to return to a system of administrative authorisation because that would require an examination of the employees' situation. There's an obligation to justify such moves and take staff rights into account."
Loss-making French carmaker Renault caused an outcry this year when it abruptly announced plans to close its Vilvoorde assembly plant in Belgium which employs 3,100 staff.
The decision, which the company confirmed last weekend, was attacked by politicians in both countries, particularly for the sudden way in which it was announced in February.
